Dome quad area regression, Darwin/ARM64, Go 1.26.10

    diagnostic_quad_cross_origin_search_test.go:78: sides=20 side=12 radius=6.033938143083053e-07 first=1.0000000000000002e-14 second=1e-14 points=[4]maths.Vec{maths.Vec{X:-1.0155281874295332e-07, Y:5.738616189901016e-07, Z:1.5637762755888684e-07}, maths.Vec{X:-1.4178449253735503e-07, Y:5.738616189901016e-07, Z:1.2109539657439408e-07}, maths.Vec{X:0, Y:6.033938143083053e-07, Z:0}, maths.Vec{X:0, Y:6.033938143083053e-07, Z:0}}

The input comes from the optical recipe's clumps-level dome: 20 sides,
side 12, opening 30 degrees, radius 6.033938143083053e-7 metres. The
second triangle collapses at the axial pole. Exact rational arithmetic
on the actual binary64 coordinates places the first triangle strictly
above the authored cross-product magnitude floor of binary64(1e-14).

Changing the cross-product subtraction origin rounds its computed
magnitude down to the floor and discards that triangle. The fixed test
uses exact squared cross magnitude, avoiding a rounded square root.

To reproduce, copy find_quad_origin_test.go into manufacture,
run go test -count=1 -v -run
'^TestDiagnosticFindQuadCrossOriginBoundary$' ./manufacture,
then remove that temporary copy. The search is retained as a producer;
the fixed regression has no search or random seed.
